blindSummary: Trans visitors to this country face severe risk. The penal code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 14 years), and an international legal-aid trust lists this country as criminalising the gender expression of trans people as well. A moratorium on prosecutions has held since 2014, but in June 2024 the constitutional court upheld the ban — a case brought in part by a local trans woman and her foreign partner — and religious leaders led nationwide anti-LGBT marches in 2023. Discrimination and violence are regular despite the moratorium.
blindOutOfScope: Prosecution moratorium is informal and revocable; the 2024 ruling keeps the statute fully alive.

Full judgment (28 June 2024): a high court upheld three penal-code provisions criminalising 'carnal knowledge against the order of nature', attempted such acts, and male-on-male gross indecency, dismissing constitutional challenges based on equality, privacy, dignity, liberty and fair-trial grounds.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: documents the July 2011 protest killings (20 dead), harsh prisons, and discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender persons.

International human-rights organisation report (Oct 2018) on arrests and violence against LGBT people in this country: documents arrests and violence against LGBT residents despite the moratorium on arrests under the criminalising laws.

LGBT-rights news platform (Dec 2015): two men arrested on homosexuality charges suffered house ransacking, assault, threats of being burned alive, extortion by community police, forced stripping, forced medical examinations and HIV/STD tests, and unauthorised distribution of their photos; an advocate at a national rights organisation asked how LGBTI people could access HIV prevention services when the same government was then making arrests against them.

LGBT-rights news platform (April 2018): coverage of police working around the moratorium on anti-gay arrests - a 24-year-old man was arrested in a provincial city and charged with 'gross indecency' under one penal-code provision rather than the others used for same-sex conduct, apparently to evade the six-year moratorium while the laws faced a constitutional challenge.
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 14 years, moratorium since 2014) — formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners; the moratorium is informal and revocable.
